### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/field-level-security.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/index.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via registerAuthzMiddleware (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ff12aed37b35ecf2cc1d8fd9a3f609fa79dfa6e7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0daefc4fb6630d9a88bb7b3c8ca993868397d51d` — the merge of head `5dea55fda88256ac633800affcc09f3ab2b9c674` into base `ff12aed37b35ecf2cc1d8fd9a3f609fa79dfa6e7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0daefc4fb6630d9a88bb7b3c8ca993868397d51d && git checkout 0daefc4fb6630d9a88bb7b3c8ca993868397d51d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ff12aed37b35ecf2cc1d8fd9a3f609fa79dfa6e7 5dea55fda88256ac633800affcc09f3ab2b9c674 && git checkout -B drift-repro ff12aed37b35ecf2cc1d8fd9a3f609fa79dfa6e7 && git merge --no-ff 5dea55fda88256ac633800affcc09f3ab2b9c674

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ff12aed37b35ecf2cc1d8fd9a3f609fa79dfa6e7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ff12aed37b35ecf2cc1d8fd9a3f609fa79dfa6e7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-addressed-writes.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/predicate-write-unreadable-not-matched.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/predicate-write-unreadable-not-matched.dogfood.test.ts, .changeset/sec-hardening-p3-write-refused-read-door.md, content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx, content/docs/permissions/permissions-matrix.mdx + none

Delta review by the same reviewer, on top of the FAIL record at `2046ac7fddadb255e49bb56cfa1f8db276978230`. Inputs: `git diff 2046ac7fdd..5dea55fda8` (one commit, 8 files, 16 / 15, prose only: docblocks, code comments, test headers, the changeset's rule bullet and the two docs sentences — no statement, type or assertion moves), the rewritten PR body read in full, and the check-runs on `5dea55fda8`. Read-only: nothing built, run or re-run. Every judgment of the earlier record that the delta does not touch stands as written there.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The must-fix is cleared.** The "What changes" sentence that stated the pre-fix path is gone; the Verification "Red before the fix" and ablation sections now carry counts, case names, the blob pair and "red, then restored" only. Re-read in full against §6: title, body, changeset, the two docs sentences, the six commit messages (the new one: "state that a write from a caller the read door refuses is refused, by id or by predicate") and every test name stay at rule level. The `Clause-②` line's "where it was admitted before" is the narrowing declaration's own wording, as the first record accepted it on the changeset. No disclosure remains.
- **The delta changes no behaviour.** Every hunk is inside a comment, a docblock, a Markdown page or the changeset body; the guard line, the call site, the return types and the tests' assertions are byte-identical to `2046ac7fdd`. The first record's ① and ④ judgments carry over unchanged.
- **Check-runs on `5dea55fda8`:** every required context `success` — `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (all eight shards), `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI`; `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI` and `Build & E2E UI` `skipped` (no `ui/` path). `Dogfood Regression Gate` is `success` with its shards `skipped`, as on the PR run before: the new dogfood file is measured by the dev's local battery, not by CI's PR run.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from the first record: `@objectstack/plugin-security` patch with `!`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The changeset's only edit is one rule sentence ("The by-id update and delete are refused too"); it adds no prescription and moves no level. `Check Changeset` is `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- §6: clear on this head (see ①).
- **Should-fix (1) of the first record is closed.** `permissions-matrix.mdx`, `authorization.mdx`, the `readUnlessRefused` docblock, the method docblock, the two code comments and both test headers now say the by-id leg "refuses" or "is refused", without naming which refusal; the unit header adds that the two legs give one answer only with no row-level policy, which is what the code does.
- **Should-fix (wording, accepted as noted):** two body sentences still equate the legs — "This is the answer the by-id update and delete already give the same caller (`callerCannotReadAddressedRow`, step 2.7)" in "What changes", and the Tests bullet "the by-id leg gives that caller the same answer as the predicate leg (control, unchanged)". The Tests bullet is true of the rig it describes (no row-level policy); the first sentence is wider than the code inside the ownership floor's domain, where the by-id leg answers the record-level `403`, as the body's own acceptance note "Two doors, two refusals, one rule" says. Reword to "is refused too", as the changeset now does. The Verification section still names `2046ac7fdd` as its head; the delta is prose only, so the readings hold, and the head's check-runs are the measurement at `5dea55fda8` — say so or leave as noted. Neither changes a contract.
- Should-fix (2) of the first record (the by-id re-read's `catch` relabelling a store fault) is a follow-up card through the seat, unchanged by the delta.
- Open questions (1) and (2) and residual (1): answered in the first record; nothing here reopens them.
- Governed surfaces: none in the file list.

### ④ Design judgment

Unchanged from the first record: the narrowing takes no declared capability away at any consumer and makes the by-id leg's rule real on the predicate leg; the break attempts there (readable-field predicate, write policy plus capability, `single`, system and run-as-system, controlled-by-parent, delegated, cap and store fault) were read in code the delta does not touch. No must-fix.
